name: US public higher education (Title II + Section 504)
standard: WCAG 2.1 AA (Title II rule); many systems also cite Section 508

laws.cite: ADA Title II, 28 CFR part 35 subpart H
laws.summary: Public colleges and universities are Title II entities, so their websites, apps, LMS course content and new social posts must meet WCAG 2.1 AA by the extended dates.

laws.cite: Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, 29 U.S.C. 794; 34 CFR part 104
laws.summary: Any institution receiving federal funds, public or private, must not exclude students with disabilities, which the Education Department's OCR applies to inaccessible websites and technology.

policy_docs.title: ED OCR - Disability Discrimination: Technology Accessibility
Colorado OIT - Digital Accessibility Law (HB21-1110) for state and local government incl. public universities

applies_to: Public universities, community colleges and state university systems (Title II and 504); private institutions via Section 504 and Title III.

deadlines.what: Title II date for institutions whose parent government has population 50,000+ (most state systems).
Title II date for institutions of small jurisdictions or special districts (e.g. some community college districts).

exceptions: Same five Title II exceptions (archived content, preexisting documents, third-party posts, individualized secured documents, preexisting social posts); course content for a specific student must still be made accessible on request/accommodation.
requires: WCAG 2.1 AA for public websites, LMS and course materials, apps and portals
Accessible procurement of ed-tech (contracts and VPAT/ACR review)

State system policies: e.g. CSU Executive Order 1111 and the Accessible Technology Initiative (coded memos AA-2013-03, AA-2015-22); Colorado HB21-1110 applies WCAG 2.1 AA to public universities with statutory damages
mobile: explicit - covered by the Title II rule's mobile app provisions.
procurement: Institution-level; CSU ATI and most state systems require accessibility review of ICT purchases.
enforcement: ED OCR complaints and resolution agreements (website accessibility is a recurring resolution topic), DOJ, private suits; state laws such as Colorado HB21-1110 add fines.
notes: CSU details (EO 1111 of 2018 superseding EO 926; coded memos) come from search result summaries of CSU campus ATI pages, not opened directly. ED OCR page URL taken from search results, not opened. The office_url for ED OCR is from general knowledge. Colorado's HB21-1110 timeline (original July 1, 2024; HB24-1454 one-year good-faith grace to July 1, 2025) from search summaries; OIT page was 403 on fetch.
